description_ru: Glaciofluvial deposits: proglacial or ice contact sand and gravel; including ice contact fans and deltas, outwash plains and terraces, pitted outwash, crevasse fillings, kames, kame terraces; commonly associated with eskers
note: GSC Map 24-1987 (Aylsworth & Shilts 1989), Glacial features around the Keewatin Ice Divide, 1:1M, 2 sheets; colour scan; description_ru holds the English legend text

description_ru: Ribbed (rogen) moraine: fields of irregular to sinuous ridges, generally < 2 km long and < 10 m high; composed mainly of till, in places sand and gravel; commonly a dense mantle of large boulders
Drumlins, flutings, and crag and tail: streamlined ridges 0.5-20 km long; generally composed of till but may be fluted bedrock or till in lee of bedrock knobs

Undifferentiated surficial materials: generally till; includes coarse and fine grained marine deposits near Arctic and southwestern Hudson Bay coast; includes minor areas of organic, fluvial, lacustrine and glaciofluvial deposits and minor areas of bedrock outcrop
note: generally till; CLIPPED at ingest to where the GSC 1:5M map says T, R or GF (marine / glaciolacustrine / organic areas keep the 1:5M class)

description_ru: Drift-poor areas: greater than 80% bedrock outcrop; includes minor areas of till or other surficial materials
